key_insight: DFT predicts that Co-, Ru-, and Y-functionalized aza-triphenylene monolayers bring hydrogen adsorption free energies closer to zero, indicating improved hydrogen evolution potential.
engineering_relevance: Transition-metal anchoring offers a route to tune two-dimensional HER catalysts, with Ru functionalization also predicted to improve carrier mobility.
method: First-principles DFT and HER volcano-plot analysis
Ab initio molecular dynamics and electronic structure/charge-transfer analysis
Climbing-image nudged elastic band calculations for Co-catalyzed reaction pathways
evidence_signal: Calculated hydrogen adsorption free energies shift from −0.78 eV for pristine aza-triphenylene to 0.05, 0.20, and 0.06 eV for Co, Ru, and Y functionalization, respectively.
watch_item: Experimental HER performance remains unverified, and the predicted 2.29 eV rate-determining Heyrovsky barrier for Co warrants kinetic validation.
paper_title: Transition Metal-Anchored Newly Synthesized Aza-Triphenylene Monolayer for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution Reaction: Insights from DFT
